cells.quote: While SJT had an effect size of less than 0.2 on early program academic results, its effect reached statistical significance (0.170; 95% CI, 0.032 to 0.308).
cells.note: The study reports a predictive association between SJT performance and early medical-program academic results, not a manipulated learning treatment; D is therefore coded as other.

cells.quote: For personality tests, the extracted effect sizes were insufficient to conduct a meta-analysis for any of the outcomes of interest.
cells.note: The study reports insufficient effect-size data for personality tests and draws no pooled-effect conclusion.

O.outcome_detail: Correlation with UCAT cognitive total as a proxy for cognitive load

result.effect: r = 0.11 for NMS SJT versus r = 0.26 for UKFP SJT

cells.quote: The scores from the UKFP SJT showed the highest degree of correlation with the UCAT cognitive total score (r = 0.26) and the NMS SJT the least (r = 0.11).
cells.note: The entry interprets the lower NMS correlation as supporting incremental validity; the study describes these correlations as a cognitive-load estimate.

O.outcome_detail: Correlation with UCAT cognitive total as a proxy for cognitive load

result.effect: r = 0.11 for NMS SJT versus r = 0.23 for UCAT SJT

cells.quote: The scores from the UKFP SJT showed the highest degree of correlation with the UCAT cognitive total score (r = 0.26) and the NMS SJT the least (r = 0.11). The UCAT SJT scores correlated 0.23 with those from the cognitive component of the assessment (p < 0.0001 in all cases).
cells.note: The study reports the NMS and UCAT correlations with cognitive measures, but does not explicitly label the comparison as a test of lower cognitive load.
